plotEn:
On February 27, 1941, James Stewart wins the Academy Award for Best Actor for his performance in The Philadelphia Story. The day after his Oscar win, Stewart receives a letter from the draft board, in which he is to report for military training. At MGM, Stewart informs Louis B. Mayer about the draft letter, who prompts to give him an "occupational deferement." However, Stewart is motivated to serve after his friend Frank Capra screens him newsreel footage of the ongoing Nazi invasion across Europe.  
Stewart returns to his childhood home in Indiana, Pennsylvania, where his father Alexander, himself a war veteran, tries to persuade him not to serve. Regardless, Stewart enlists as a combat pilot in the U.S. Army Air Force. He arrives for training at Moffett Field, where he meets U.S. Army Colonel Terrill. There, Stewart appears in a short film, Winning Your Wings, to help recruit airmen. 
In 1943, Stewart leaves to serve in the European theater, which will fly B-24s from RAF Tibenham as part of the 445th Operations Group over Europe. As the squadron's commanding officer, Stewart is warned that a German U-boat has been spotted over the Atlantic, which shoots down the low-flying "Sunflower Sue." Stewart continues flying on to his base, in England, concerned that lingering around the crash site will endanger the remaining aircraft in the formation. Subsequent search and rescue efforts fail to locate the fourteen man crew.
